items.title: The canonical map from the normalised to the associated complex is a morphism of complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file simplicial.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-map-associated-complexes at source lines 3996-4002: for a simplicial object U of an abelian category the canonical maps N(U_n) to U_n assemble into a morphism of complexes N(U) to s(U). The proof at source lines 4004-4010 is a direct computation with the differentials: on s(U)_n the differential is the alternating sum of the face maps, the face maps with i smaller than n vanish on the normalised subobject, and what remains is exactly the boundary map of N(U) by definition. It is short; the substance is the observation that all but one term of the alternating sum dies on N, which is the definitional reason the two differentials agree.
